recall_prompt: Say how you would find the middle terms — why an odd n gives two of them and which two, and what each comes to.
insider_note: n = 17 is odd, so there are TWO middle terms, the 9th and the 10th, and each has its own ¹⁷Cᵣ. Answering only T₉ is the standard half answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Decide which terms are the middle
steps.margin_note: First mark. n = 17 is odd, so there are TWO middle terms: the (n + 1)/2 = 9th and the next, the 10th.
steps.memory_tip: n = 17 is odd, so there are TWO middle terms, the 9th and the 10th.
lines: n = 17 is odd, so there are two middle terms:
the (n + 1)/2 = 9th and the 10th, T₉ and T₁₀

recall.must_convey: That n = 17 is odd, so the two middle terms are T₉ and T₁₀.
accept: n is seventeen which is odd so there are two middle terms, the ninth and the tenth
odd n gives two middle terms n plus one by two and the next
the middle terms are T nine and T ten
n seventeen odd kabatti two middle terms, ninth and tenth
seventeen plus one by two is nine so the ninth and tenth

steps.why: With n odd there are n + 1 = 18 terms, an even count, so two terms share the middle.

steps.label: Evaluate both
steps.margin_note: Second mark. T₉ has r = 8, T₁₀ has r = 9. Powers of x: 2·9 + 3·8 = 42 and 2·8 + 3·9 = 43.
steps.memory_tip: T₉ has r = 8 and T₁₀ has r = 9, each with its own ¹⁷Cᵣ. Powers of x: 42 and 43.

recall.must_convey: That T₉ = ¹⁷C₈·4⁹·5⁸·x⁴² and T₁₀ = ¹⁷C₉·4⁸·5⁹·x⁴³.
accept: T nine is seventeen C eight four to the nine five to the eight x to the forty two and T ten is seventeen C nine four to the eight five to the nine x to the forty three
r eight gives the ninth term and r nine gives the tenth
the powers of x are forty two and forty three
T nine seventeen C eight four power nine five power eight x power forty two, T ten seventeen C nine four power eight five power nine x power forty three
two terms with x to the forty two and forty three

steps.why: Each middle term is one r-step from the other; the powers of x rise by one because x³ replaces one x².
common_mistakes: Adding only the bracket powers as 9 + 8 = 17, forgetting the 2 and the 3 from x² and x³ — the power is 2·9 + 3·8 = 42.
